newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq completes pilgrims' flights via no-go zones.
newsitem.headline: Iraq completes pilgrims' flights via no-go zones.

text.p: Iraqi helicopters, defying the West's no-fly zones, on Sunday completed the transfer of Moslem pilgrims returning from Saudi Arabia, the official Iraqi News Agency (INA) reported.

"Iraqi helicopters have safely completed transporting sick and elderly Iraqi pilgrims from Arar in the border between Iraq and Saudi Arabia to their areas of residence in Baghdad and the provinces," it said.
Earlier, the agency said several helicopters flying pilgrims had landed safely in the "provinces of Baghdad, Anbar, Saladdin, Dhiqar, Meisan and Basra".

It said helicopters flying pilgrims from Arar landed safely in Mosul on Saturday. The city is 400 km (250 miles) north of Baghdad and well inside the northern no-fly zone policed by U.S. and British planes based in Turkey.
Iraq's Minister of Endowment and Religious Affairs Abdul- Muneim Ahmed Saleh was among the Iraqi pilgrims who visited Saudi Arabia.
"Our aim is to alleviate suffering of some pilgrims because of the long land road between our border with Saudi Arabia and their homes," Saleh told Reuters TV in Arar.
INA did not say how many pilgrims were transported.
Some 1,100 pilgrims went to Mecca from Iraq this year for the Moslem haj pilgrimage, but it said it would only fly back the sick and elderly.
Last week Iraq sent nine helicopters to the Saudi border in defiance of the U.S. and allied ban on flights in the area.
Washington said it would not obstruct the flights but warned Baghdad against massing troops in southern Iraq.
Iraq does not recognise the no-fly zones set up to protect rebel Kurds in the north against attacks by Iraqi armed forces and dissident Shi'ite Moslems in the south against Iraqi air attacks.

The helicopter flights represented a renewed challenge this month to the longstanding flight restrictions. Iraq flew a civilian plane to Saudi Arabia on April 9 carrying 104 elderly and sick pilgrims to Mecca. It returned the same day.
